findings.element: 2026 Consensus Brackets table — 'Key View' column
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column text is visibly cut off for multiple rows (Goldman Sachs, BCA Research, IBRC/Stanford, Blue Chip Consensus). Full commentary is truncated mid-sentence with no ellipsis or overflow handling, making the content unreadable in a board context.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary bullet points
findings.detail: Several sector KPI tiles (e.g., Passenger Airlines, Restaurants & Food Svcs, Grocery & Food Retail, Residential Real Estate) have bullet-point commentary text that is cut off at the tile boundary, with sentences ending abruptly mid-word or mid-phrase.

findings.element: Sector KPI tiles — body commentary text
findings.detail: The bullet-point commentary text inside all sector tiles (Passenger Airlines, Hotels, Restaurants, etc.) is rendered at an extremely small font size — estimated 7–8px — making it effectively illegible at normal viewing distance for a board deck.

findings.element: 2026 Consensus Brackets table — source footnote
findings.detail: The sources line at the bottom of the consensus table is rendered in very small, low-contrast gray text that is difficult to read without zooming in.

findings.element: Bottom synthesis section — six-theme bullet points
findings.detail: The six numbered synthesis paragraphs at the bottom of the tab are rendered in very small body text (estimated 8–9px). For a CEO/board audience reading a deck, this density and size would be flagged as illegible.

findings.element: Quarterly GDP bar chart — subtitle/annotation text
findings.detail: The chart subtitle referencing 'tariff shutdown noise' and the 'So what' annotation text below the chart appear to be clipped at the right edge of the panel container.

findings.element: Outlook tab — 'So what' commentary blocks
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary notes appear below the charts they reference (Quarterly GDP chart and Consensus Indicators chart) rather than preceding the first chart on the tab. Per style_guide §1, fc-note commentary must precede the first chart.

findings.element: Sector KPI tiles grid — Federal Government and Freight & Logistics row
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector tiles (Federal Government, Freight & Logistics) contains only 2 tiles versus 5 tiles in the rows above, leaving a large blank area to the right. This creates a visibly unbalanced grid layout that would appear unfinished in a board presentation.

findings.element: Sector KPI tiles — vertical spacing between tile rows
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the first and second rows of sector tiles appears noticeably larger than the gap between subsequent rows, creating inconsistent panel spacing relative to peer panels.

findings.element: Week 47 top commentary block
findings.detail: The opening commentary paragraph contains hedging language ('could provide temporary offsets') and runs as a single dense block exceeding 4 sentences, violating the 2–4 sentence rule for fc-note commentary blocks.

findings.element: Sector-level mini bar charts — axis labels and growth figures
findings.detail: The year labels (e.g., '22, '23, '24, '25), GDP-share percentages, and annual growth figures inside every sector panel are rendered at an extremely small point size (estimated 6–7 pt). At board-deck zoom levels these are unreadable without magnification.

findings.element: Bottom data-source footnote line
findings.detail: The full-width footnote at the very bottom of the tab ('Sources: BEA GDP PCE; BLS CPI, Jobs…') is rendered in a font size that is illegible at normal viewing scale, violating the minimum contrast/size requirement for attribution text.

findings.element: Annual-chart data-vintage / methodology note bar (below filter row)
findings.detail: The grey metadata strip ('ANNUAL CHART DATA VINTAGE … SEE METHODOLOGY §F') is set in a very small, low-contrast grey font that is effectively illegible at dashboard resolution.

findings.element: EX 2 commentary headline ('Real GDP held 2.0% in 2025…')
findings.detail: The EX 2 section header and its associated table appear without a preceding fc-note commentary block above the table. The style guide requires the fc-note to precede the first chart/table in each exhibit section.

findings.element: Sector panel commentary text (multiple panels, e.g., Commercial RE, Pharma/Biotech, Chips/Hardware)
findings.detail: Several sector-panel commentary lines are clipped mid-sentence at the bottom edge of their container (text ends abruptly with no ellipsis), indicating the text box height is insufficient for the copy.

findings.element: Bottom two sector rows (Cruise Lines / Travel Agencies) vs. upper sector rows
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector panels (Cruise Lines, Travel Agencies) has noticeably more vertical whitespace below it before the EX 2 table than the spacing between any other sector rows, creating an inconsistent rhythm.

findings.element: EX 1 GDP Commentary block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains five sentences, exceeding the maximum of four sentences permitted by the style guide. The opening clause ('Real GDP at 3.4% annualized is a strong print that creates a misleading picture…') also uses hedging framing ('misleading picture') that borders on editorialising rather than factual narration.

findings.element: Jobs tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Unemployment tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Exhibit 2 — Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker line chart axis labels and data point labels
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and the small percentage labels on the data points are extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard viewing size. Senior reviewers would struggle to verify values without zooming in.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector wage growth horizontal bar chart y-axis sector labels
findings.detail: The sector name labels on the y-axis of the bar chart are very small and several appear truncated or barely legible (e.g., 'Hotel Front Desk / Hou...', 'Z-Commerce (Warehouse)', 'Grocery Store (Avg)'). At board-deck resolution these would be unreadable.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector wage growth bar chart y-axis labels
findings.detail: Several sector labels appear to be cut off mid-word (e.g., 'Hotel Front Desk / Hou...' instead of full label), indicating the label container is too narrow for the text.

findings.element: Source footnotes beneath Exhibit 2 and Exhibit 5 table
findings.detail: Source and methodology footnote text is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears sub-8px), making it effectively illegible without zooming. While footnotes are secondary, they are still visible elements on a board-facing dashboard.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Real wages annual chart subtitle/caption text
findings.detail: The subtitle line beneath the Exhibit 3 chart title ('Atlanta Fed WGT 3MMA — Annual Unweighted Median Hourly...') is rendered at very small size and is difficult to parse at normal viewing distance.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary — Nominal vs Real (fc-note panel)
findings.detail: The commentary block contains five sentences, exceeding the maximum of 4 sentences permitted per style_guide §2. The passage also contains hedging language ('essentially zero', 'look resilient') which style_guide §2 flags as forbidden filler.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Real wages annual bar/line chart
findings.detail: The chart plots two series (Nominal and Real/inflation-adjusted) but the legend indicators are extremely small and low-contrast, making it difficult to distinguish which line/bar corresponds to which series without close inspection. The legend is present but effectively non-functional at board viewing size.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — 'Annual CPI is still well above the Fed's 2% target after three years'
findings.detail: The chart area between the title/subtitle and the source note is completely blank. No bars or data are rendered despite the source note referencing BLS series CUUR0000AA0 and describing a bar chart of dec-to-dec YoY % change.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — 'Goods inflation has normalised; services and shelter remain sticky' (left panel)
findings.detail: The chart area is entirely blank. No grouped bars or data series are visible between the subtitle and the source note.

findings.element: Exhibit 6 — 'Category-level annual rates show four still above 3%' (right panel)
findings.detail: The chart area is entirely blank. No sortable bar chart or data is rendered despite the source note referencing BLS CPI-U category data.

findings.element: Exhibit 7 — 'Trimmed-mean and median CPI track headline — inflation is broad, not concentrated'
findings.detail: The chart area is entirely blank. A legend with four series (Headline CPI MoM, Trimmed-Mean CPI, Median CPI, Fed 2% Target) is visible but no lines are plotted in the chart body.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — 'Energy and transport categories are pulling the basket higher' (right panel)
findings.detail: The chart area appears blank or nearly blank. A legend referencing Sep'26 accelerating, Sep'26 cooling, and Aug'26 is present but no bar data is visible in the chart body.

findings.element: All exhibit subtitles, axis labels, and source notes throughout the tab
findings.detail: Subtitle rows, axis tick labels, and source/footnote text are rendered at an extremely small size (appears sub-8px at dashboard resolution), making them unreadable without zooming. This would be illegible on a projected board slide.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 'So what' commentary block (right panel)
findings.detail: The 'So what' interpretive note appears below the (empty) chart area rather than preceding the first chart on the panel, violating the requirement that fc-note commentary precede the first chart.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Energy and transport categories chart (right panel)
findings.detail: The legend items (Sep'26 accelerating, Sep'26 cooling, Aug'26) are present in the header but with the chart body empty it is impossible to verify that legend colors match the plotted series, and no series are actually visible to confirm the mapping.

findings.element: EX 2 dual-axis line chart — axis labels and data point annotations
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and the small percentage annotations on both the Case-Shiller YoY line and the 30yr Mortgage Rate line are rendered at a font size that is extremely difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale. Senior reviewers would struggle to verify the data values without zooming in.

findings.element: EX 3 Home prices doubled chart — x-axis year labels
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels (1988–2021) are rendered at a very small size and are barely legible, making it impossible to read specific time periods without zooming.

findings.element: EX 4 Mortgage rate gap to Fed funds chart — axis labels and data point markers
findings.detail: Year labels on the x-axis and percentage labels on the y-axis are extremely small and low-contrast against the background, making them illegible at normal viewing distance for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: EX 5 Housing starts bar chart — x-axis year labels
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels spanning 1990–2025 are rendered at a font size too small to read clearly, and the bar labels/values are not discernible at dashboard scale.

findings.element: EX 6 Affordability index dual-panel chart — axis labels and bar annotations
findings.detail: Both the affordability index values and the months-supply values on the lower panel are rendered at a font size that is illegible at normal viewing scale. The y-axis tick labels are particularly hard to read.

findings.element: Footer source citations (bottom of page)
findings.detail: The source attribution text at the very bottom of the dashboard is rendered at an extremely small size, well below readable threshold even for footnote-level text. While sources are expected to be small, this appears to fall below the minimum legible size.

findings.element: EX 7 Metro table — Trend column arrows
findings.detail: The 'Falling' trend labels in the Trend column appear tightly packed and the arrow icons and text risk overlapping with adjacent column content at this render size, particularly for rows with longer metro names.

findings.element: EX 2 'So what' callout text
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary reads: 'Rates need to break below ~5.5% to unlock the lock-in cohort — until then transaction volume stays compressed and price discovery is thin.' This is a single sentence, falling below the minimum of 2 sentences required by the style guide.

findings.element: EX 4 'So what' callout text
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary for the mortgage rate gap panel appears to be a single sentence ('Fed cuts don't automatically translate to mortgage relief — the long-end + MBS spread is the binding constraint, not the policy rate'), which is below the minimum 2-sentence requirement.

findings.element: EX 2 dual-axis line chart
findings.detail: The chart uses two separate y-axes (Case-Shiller YoY % and 30yr Mortgage Rate %) on different scales. While labels appear in the subtitle text, there is no clearly visible in-chart legend box distinguishing the two series by color at a glance, which is a readability risk for a board audience.

findings.element: EX 3 and EX 4 side-by-side panels vs. EX 5 and EX 6 side-by-side panels
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the EX 3/EX 4 panel row and the EX 5/EX 6 panel row appears slightly tighter than the spacing between the top commentary section and the EX 2 full-width chart, creating inconsistent rhythm across the tab.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker — Daily Closes chart (F5), axis labels and annotations
findings.detail: X-axis date labels and several inline annotations on the daily closes chart are rendered at a font size that is too small to read at dashboard viewing scale, making the time series context unclear for a board-level audience.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain panel (F6) — node detail rows
findings.detail: The descriptive sub-text beneath each node label (e.g., 'Awaiting next official CPI release') is rendered at an extremely small font size, well below readable threshold for a CEO-level deck.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary block
findings.detail: The body commentary paragraph in Section 4 is rendered in a very small font size relative to the panel width, making it difficult to read without zooming in, which is inappropriate for board-level presentation.

findings.element: Chart F7 — Every major oil shock since 1973, x-axis and y-axis labels
findings.detail: Year labels on the x-axis and price labels on the y-axis are extremely small and difficult to read at normal viewing distance, undermining the chart's communicative value.

findings.element: Chart F8 — Past shocks table, body text in Economic Consequence column
findings.detail: The economic consequence descriptions in the rightmost column of the historical shocks table are rendered at a very small font size, making them illegible without zooming.

findings.element: Section 3 — Sector Impact table, source footnote
findings.detail: The source/disclaimer footnote beneath the sector sensitivity table is rendered at a font size that is effectively unreadable at board presentation scale.

findings.element: Chart F3 — Three oil shocks in 25 years, x-axis year labels
findings.detail: Year labels along the x-axis appear crowded and partially overlap each other across the full date range (1998–2025+), reducing readability of the time axis.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary
findings.detail: The commentary contains hedging language ('causality is debated,' 'still evolving') and qualifiers that dilute the analytical signal. Style guide requires direct, hedge-free language in fc-note commentary.

findings.element: Section 2 panels (F5 Oil Supply Shock Tracker vs F6 Full Oil Impact Chain)
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the Section 2 header and the two side-by-side panels appears noticeably tighter than the spacing used in Section 1 and Section 3, creating an inconsistent rhythm across sections.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain panel (F6) — Phase indicator row
findings.detail: The 'PHASES ACTIVE' counter widget (showing '0 of 3 transmitting') appears misaligned relative to the SHOCK and ELAPSED metric tiles to its left, sitting at a different vertical baseline.
